name: text-ops
title: String operations
summary: A contact card built from three raw exported strings: textTransform capitalises the name, takes an upper-case initial and upper-cases the role, textMeasure sizes the role pill, textSubtext trims a preview and textLength counts its characters.
prompt: A contact card from raw strings: "ada lovelace" shown as "Ada Lovelace" with an initial avatar, the role upper-cased in a pill that fits the text, and a 30-character preview of a message with its length.
teaches: Transform a string into a new text variable with textTransform {text, start, len, operation, varName}: 1 lower, 2 upper, 3 trim, 4 capitalise words, 5 capitalise first; len -1 runs to the end
Cut a substring with textSubtext {text, start, len, varName} and add an ellipsis with textMerge
Measure the rendered width with textMeasure (mode 0) after setting the paint's textSize, and size a pill with it: right = 122 + @roleW
Count characters with textLength {text, name} and print the count with textFromFloat
pitfalls: The JSON names for textTransform's operation are off by one in the reference parser: "uppercase" writes 1 (TEXT_TO_LOWERCASE), "lowercase" 2 (upper), "capitalize" 3 (trim). Write the number
textMeasure measures with the paint as it is at that point in the commands: set textSize first
textSubtext throws past the end of the string on Java (substring): keep start + len within the text, or use len -1
These operations are in the AndroidX profile: the header needs profiles 513 (the Java writer refuses opcode 199 without it)

A card drawn to x = 348 only fits the header width: draw it to componentWidth() - 12, and when the fixed-size text (a 21 px name, a 30-character preview) would no longer fit, scale the canvas down as a whole

snippets.note: start 0, len 1, operation 2: the upper-case initial

check.describe: A purple circle with A, "Ada Lovelace", a teal ANALYST pill fitted to its text, and the preview "The engine might compose elabo…" over "50 characters". Resized, the card fills the live width (right edge at componentWidth() - 12) with the divider following it; below the 360 design width the whole card is scaled down (@s = min(1, w / 360)) so the name and the preview stay inside it, at 234 wide too.
